title: World-wide High-speed Rail Tycoon
selectCity: Choose a city on the map or in the list.
hint: Your Tokyo–Nagoya starter service is ready to earn revenue. Advance a month, tune fares in Services, or compare two new construction opportunities in Build a line.
reportHint: Tickets are collected when a month closes. Construction and grants are capital flows, separate from operating profit.
noReport: Advance a month to close your first report.
soundless: This early build has no sound.
stale_revision: The game changed. Review the latest state and try again.
storage_failed: Could not save. Your previous game is intact. Free some space and retry.
invalid_save: The saved game is invalid or belongs to a different build. It has been preserved.
locked: This game is open in another tab. Close that tab and reload here.
storageUnavailable: Local storage is unavailable. Enable storage for this site and reload.
action_limit: This development game has reached its action limit. Export your snapshot to keep it.
buildHint: When the line opens, lease trains here and apply a service plan to earn revenue.
estimateNote: Scenario engineering estimates. Tunnels cost more; detours take longer.
no_route: No authored alignment for this pair. Choose a listed construction opportunity.
already_built: This line is public, owned, or already under construction.
insufficient_cash: Not enough cash. Review financing in Company.
line_not_open: This line is still under construction.
invalid_service: Use 0–16 return trips/day and a USD 10–300 one-way fare.
fleet_shortage: Lease enough trains on this corridor or reduce frequency.
fleet_in_use: Reduce frequency before returning this train.
fleet_limit: The fleet limit is 32 trains; cash must be nonnegative.
loan_limit: The development loan limit is USD 5B.
cash_limit: This action exceeds the development cash limit.
set_service: Service plan saved for the next month.
advance_year: Twelve business months resolved and saved.
serviceHint: One return trip means one departure each way. Trains stay on this corridor. Set frequency to 0 to suspend service.
forecastCosts: Operating costs, required leases and line upkeep
loanTerms: Borrow any amount within the remaining USD 5B credit limit at 2% annual interest. Cash overdrafts incur 1% monthly interest. Borrowing always requires your action.
noServices: No services on this corridor yet.
draft_not_applied: Service draft is not applied. Apply or restore the current plan before advancing.
invalid_loan_amount: Enter a positive USD amount with up to two decimal places.
terrainCredits: Terrain: Mapzen / USGS; water: Natural Earth
hokkaidoMountainWhy: The shorter northern approach crosses the Oshima and Shiribeshi uplands: this scenario needs 170 km of tunnel.
hokkaidoValleyWhy: The longer coastal/Chitose approach skirts the central uplands. It still needs 45 km of tunnel; the detour is not mountain-free.
kansaiMountainWhy: A shorter crossing through the highlands west of Lake Biwa; this scenario needs 140 km of tunnel.
kansaiValleyWhy: The longer route follows Lake Biwa’s eastern and southern shores instead of crossing the lake. This scenario still needs 20 km of tunnel.
idleExplanation: These lines earn no fares while upkeep and lease costs continue. Review Services, lease trains if needed, and apply a service.
idleNeedsTrains: Lease trains and apply a service.
idleNeedsService: Trains are leased. Apply a service with a frequency above zero.
newGameWarning: This replaces your current company and save, including all lines, loans, trains and reports. This cannot be undone.
newGameStart: Start in East Asia in January 2029 with USD 100 million and an active Tokyo–Nagoya service. Display preferences are kept.
fundingFormula: Your contribution − cash available + any cash deficit = additional cash needed (minimum USD 0).
fundingNegativeCash: Your cash balance is negative, so this includes clearing the existing deficit.
fundingLoanHelp: Borrow funding shortfall takes this full amount in one loan. You can enter a different loan amount below.
fundingChoosePlan: Choose an unbuilt line in Build a line to see its funding breakdown.
shortfallInterest: Monthly interest added by borrowing the full gap
stationHandling: Station handling / passenger journey · both ends
directService: A direct service runs between this city pair. Another corridor needs its own service.
stationAbsent: No station yet · included when a new line opens
stationPackage: Basic endpoint station works open with this project and are included in this introductory package. No separate station order is needed.
helpFirstMonth: Your starter trains are ready. Advance one month to collect fares and see a reconciled report. You can also plan a new line immediately.
helpIdle: An open line has no running service. Review it, lease trains if needed, and apply a positive frequency to start earning fares.
helpPair: Choose two different cities. The listed opportunities have reviewed alignments; both cities can start without stations or an existing network.
helpConstruction: Track and endpoint station works open together on the stated date. Each month also settles your operating costs and income.
helpOpen: This line and its stations are ready. Review its service, lease the required trains, and apply a fare and frequency.
helpPublic: This public line is already operational. You can lease trains and run a service without buying the track.
helpFunding: Compare the engineering and funding breakdown. Company financing can cover the full displayed shortfall in one loan.
helpBuildReady: Your cash covers the construction contribution. Starting construction commits the project package and its stated opening date.
helpFleet: Lease trains on this corridor before applying its service. Trains on another corridor are not assigned here.
helpDraft: These are draft settings. Check the fleet requirement and forecast, then apply the plan or restore the saved settings before advancing.
helpSuspended: Frequency zero suspends this service. Any leased trains and owned-line upkeep still cost money; resume service or return spare trains.
helpOperating: This plan is saved for the next month. Advancing collects fares and posts track access, station handling, train leases and running costs.
helpLoss: This month’s operating costs exceeded ticket income. Review service demand, fares, fleet and idle-line costs before advancing again.
helpReport: The report separates ticket income and operating costs from loans, grants and construction. Closing cash reconciles all of them.
helpFinance: The funding preview names its route and alignment. Review that route to change the plan; borrowing is a separate explicit action.
helpCompany: Company finances are shared by every line. Services show what your fleet can earn before company-wide interest.
helpExplore: Inspect stations and compare the build opportunities. A new city pair can operate independently of your existing railway.
helpFinished: This campaign is complete. Company lets you start a new game.
helpFunded: Your cash covers this construction package. Review the route, then start construction when you are ready.
helpBuiltOperating: This line and its stations are open, with a saved running service. Review its fares, frequency and fleet as demand changes.
